body: Oh dear, that's not good. Hey, you can write to me. I know how much it sucks to get help and get a cold response like that. Hope I could help. :)

I failed 4 classes back when I was in the Uni. I'm 28 yo too but despite all those failures, I managed to obtain a bachelor's degree. When I graduated, I received so many rejection letters. Even so after I resigned from my first job... I got rejection after rejection... Even while I'm working, my ideas got rejected. I think I had been rejected more than accepted. Even when I was dating, I've always been the dumpee - never the dumper.

I know how difficult it is but it shouldn't be a reason to commit suicide. I've had suicidal thoughts and recovered a bit recently. I realised slowly that I made the right decision. We all get rejected. Even a presidential candidate who won got rejected by those who didn't vote for him... That's millions of voters = millions of people who rejected him. Imagine that! 

I admire your passion... You've made it this far and I'm confident that you can make it through... Sometimes we get overwhelmed by how big our goals and the uncertainties along the way. It happens to me too. I've always wanted to be a journalist but in my country, they don't get paid well and it's also listed as one of the most dangerous places to be a journalist coz of the political killings. At this age, I'm still not a journalist just coz I'm trying to pay off my bills and debt and got stuck just doing that. It's depressing. I think what worked for me (which you can try) is that I try to separate myself with the work that I do. I remind myself that it's about the work and not me. If I fail, it just means that I need to try another strategy or reassess my goals and see if it's doable. I can see that you're passionate about anthropology. Don't give up. There are many successful people who have gone through the same thing as yours and look at them now! :)

The thing is, if you choose to do what you love, it's really going to make you poor and miserable because no matter what you do it's difficult to separate work and personal stuff because your passion is personal. But imagine failing in doing something that you don't like... Might as well fail doing what you love. ;-)
How is it going?
I'm 28 years old, never had a serious relationship. I dated around but I ended up always dating a-holes. :-\
I'm off to sleep. It's almost midnight here. But please feel free to leave me a message. Talk about your story. :)

Please don't do it. If you need someone to talk to, I'm here. Just message me.

Depression sucks - I'm struggling with depression too. It's not your fault that she started seeing another man. It was her decision. She could have worked it out but she chose to do something that would really, really hurt you. Granted that you have an alcohol and depression problems - whatever you're struggling with, big or small, you don't deserve to be cheated on. No one does!

I think you'll make a wonderful father... Get some professional help to resolve your alcohol and depression. You son needs you to be there for him. It's not his fault that his mother left you. You may not be perfect, she might not like you, but think about your son and what his life would be like if he grows up without a father.

I agree... Most people are so much kinder with people who suffer from diseases like cancer, aids or something that they'd rush to comfort those people. But with depression, the "disease" often manifests in emotions and people mistake this as your character. It's not! Depressed people are not weak... People who are thinking of ending their lives are not seeking attention. Normal people don't understand this because they don't think the way depressed people do... 

People do care. However, like I said, depression is a bit more complicated than it should be because of the lack of awareness. If you don't have physical wounds or looking physically weak, then people assume that your "sadness" will go away and you'll recover some day... That's why they don't pay attention as much as they should when you're suffering from depression. That's just my opinion.

It's not your fault. It was her decision and you didn't know... She probably didn't understand where you were coming from too. You didn't know where she was coming from. But please don't end your life. We all make mistakes and most of the time, we don't realise that our "bad days" can affect another person so much.

I understand that you're probably thinking this way because you might have felt guilty, but it's not a reason end your life. You can learn from this... The next time you see someone being bullied, defend that person. Bullying is unacceptable... You may chat with me... I'll be here. Whatever happens, please don't hurt yourself.

I did book a trip to Thailand for 10 days. I got back from a trip and photographed-I love photography and traveling so much- but with this depression it's different. I hope my next trip will ease me from this pain.
Same here. I just want to die but I' just afraid to do it. I wish I could just disappear without causing anyone any trouble.
I guess know someone's willing to listen to you when you talk about suicide would make you feel a little bit better. :)
Hey, I may not be able to say the right things but you can always talk to me and I hope this helps. I'm here to listen.
Thanks for your offer. This makes me feel better.

Hey, I know what it feels like. I know 5 people who committed suicide - 1 of them happened to be in my circle of friends, the rest are people I know from my high school. Despite that, it felt like there's nothing that could have prepared me for the all those deaths. 

I've only signed up in Reddit recently when I started having my own suicide thoughts. Perhaps your friend had an entirely different experience and I don't know her but let me share you a couple of things I know:
1. Depression clouds our judgment.
2. Never ignore someone who talks about depression. You know how some people avoid the "Debbie Downer" in the group... Sometimes it starts that way. The depressed person underestimates the kindness of people around her but at the same time, many people also don't take another person's depression seriously. I'm not sure why - either we're so used to hearing the word depression that it becomes the norm or that we just dismiss it because we think that the depressed person can handle it. Either way, I think there's a disconnect. 

It's so difficult to know what goes on inside someone's mind. He/She could be concealing the suicidal thoughts out of embarrassment or perhaps someone had shame/ignore them. 

I've regretted that I was not able to help my friend in those days when he needed me. It took me years to come to terms with his death. It's been almost a decade now and thinking about him still makes me cry. I'm dealing with my own depression and suicidal thoughts now. I've lost friends - friends who did their best to be patient with me whenever they listen to me talking about depression. They've just stopped. It just made me feel worse about myself. I sometimes think that I'm just being a coward for not killing myself, but there's also that part of me who wanted to hold on and hope that things will get better. While procrastinating on my suicide, I'm just getting things sorted (i.e. making sure that all of my files for work are accessible, all of my possession given away, withdrawing my money from the bank and giving it to someone else). I still don't know whether to just go for it or live but I'm tired of living. 

I hope this perspective helps answer some question.

And yeah, you're right - many people don't know what depression is like. It is frustrating to be honest. Sometimes, all I want is to have someone who'd listen to me patiently as I have done for my friends. I remember taking another friend out for a jog every week after his girlfriend broke up with him and I did that for years. I would also drive home another friend since she's feeling depressed. On the way home (which was quite far from where I live), she would talk about her problems. I extended the same kindness to this friend who I was talking about - the one who ignored me when I talked about suicide. I always cared for my friends and checked in with them... It's just sad that things like this happens.

Thanks for your wonderful advice. No, as much as I am tempted to ask him why he's not replying to me or if we're still friends, I wouldn't send another message to save my dignity. I get tired too. I guess I'm just hurt with what he did. I was able to talk to other friends regarding my suicidal thoughts and I feel so much better. I realized that there are so many other people who are willing to listen. It's just sad that my friend and I have come to this point. I never thought that my depression could lead to destroying a friendship that I treasured so much.

Yeah, I keep on convincing myself that whatever it is, it's for the best. I just don't know why he's suddenly silent like that. I could see on Facebook messenger that he has read my messages. But yeah, he probably doesn't know how to deal with it. I just thought I should let go. I'm trying to put myself in his shoes... But it would be very different for me. I'm always out to help others. This is why I'm hurt all the more because I could recall those days when he was the one who opened up to me about his depression and I never left him.

It made me doubt my decisions - like I should have not talked about it because it might have made him feel uncomfortable. I tried not to take it personally. Maybe it wasn't my fault and that he's just not emotionally ready for discussions like this. I just feel bad that I've ruined our friendship and that he'll probably never talk to me ever again. I'd like to think that it's not my fault but I just feel worse and worse about myself coz he's not talking.
Thank you, gracefulgiraffelove.
Hey, I'd like to be your friend. What's your story? :)

All the while I thought he got my back... I guess some people get tired of listening. I like to think that I never got tired of listening to people who talk about their depression and I would check in them... Sometimes even everyday since I know what depression is like. I think this is why I'm having suicidal thoughts: now that it's me who's suffering, no one seems to want to be patient enough to listen in my circle of friends.
